planner_heuristic_statement: Dual-Track Lineage and Executable Verification Heuristic (DT-LEV): 1. Separation of Epistemological Layers: Historical facts (verbatim commits, code diffs, logs, file presence) must remain distinct from semantic interpretations (inferred intent, requirement meaning, evaluation claims); truth decisions regarding active requirement status must strictly derive from cited facts through explicit interpretive arguments. 2. Orthogonality of Lifecycle and Implementation: Requirement lifecycle status (Active vs. Superseded vs. Partially Superseded) is orthogonal to implementation state (Implemented, Partial, Unimplemented, Unenforced). A requirement superseded by a subsequent user instruction creates zero present corrective work regardless of whether it was ever implemented historically. 3. Normative Implementation Target: The normative target consists solely of active, surviving user requirements. Current machine behavior must be established strictly from executable runtime source code, deterministic workflow definitions, active configuration files, and persisted structural behaviors—never inferred merely from specification documents (e.g., Agents.md), filenames, or model self-reports. 4. Corrective Gap Principle: An outstanding defect constitutes actionable present corrective work if and only if the underlying user requirement survives active today and today's executable machine fails to deterministically implement or enforce it.
